audit.whatIsWrong: content.win reads Cassiopeia / Skill / Rumble / Rumble / Cassiopeia / Rumble / Rumble — it hands Rumble four stages in a lane Cassiopeia wins 60.78% of over 102 games, and it contradicts its own whys, every one of which gives the stage to Cassiopeia except level 6. CHAMP_FULL.phases reads Skill / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Skill / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia.
audit.why: The mirror audit at audits/top/rumble__cassiopeia.json reached the same conclusion from the other side and for the same reason: her damage is a 0.75s Twin Fang chained off 3.5s Noxious Blast poison that scales forever, his is a 600-range cone that needs her to stand still. There is no stage where Rumble out-duels that. Level 6 as the one even row is right.
audit.corrected: content.win should follow CHAMP_FULL.phases. Not proposed as edits — single-word side values cannot move inside the length band.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike calls The Equalizer "his one real threat" and "a long cooldown" without ever giving the number, and it names the ability "His Equalizer".
audit.why: The Equalizer is 130/105/80. On a 130-second cooldown at rank 1, baiting it out is not a small edge — it is more than two minutes in which Rumble has nothing that touches a kiting Cassiopeia, and the reader should be counting it.
audit.corrected: 130s written into spikes[1].text, wants.you[2] and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) wants.you[1], mid, late and whys[6] all build the plan on Miasma grounding or cancelling Rumble's escape. Rumble has no dash and no movement ability — grounding removes nothing from his kit. What actually keeps him out of Flamespitter range is Miasma's slow. (b) late and whys[6] credit a "Q slow"; Noxious Blast has no slow, it grants Cassiopeia move speed. (c) wants.foe[1] says he wants an "overheat-empowered Flamespitter". Overheating is his penalty state, not his buff state — at 100% Heat he cannot cast spells at all. The buff is Danger Zone at 50% Heat, and Overheat is the biggest free window in the lane.
audit.why: Riot: Junkyard Titan — "When he reaches 50% Heat he reaches Danger Zone, granting all his basic abilities bonus effects. When he reaches 100% Heat, he starts Overheating... making him unable to cast spells for a few seconds." Rumble's kit file lists no dash; the mirror audit states the same. Noxious Blast — "granting her increased Move Speed if she hits an enemy champion", no slow. Miasma is what slows.
audit.corrected: Grounding demoted to the slow in wants.you[1], mid, late and whys[6]; the phantom Q slow removed; Danger Zone and the Overheat cast-lockout written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: "His Equalizer" in spikes[1].text and "Twin Fangs" plural in mid.
audit.why: The abilities are The Equalizer and Twin Fang.

edits.before: His Equalizer (R) is his one real threat — two angled lines of fire that zone you off a wave or burst you if you stand in them; everything else you beat.
edits.after: The Equalizer (R) is his one real threat — a wall of fire on a 130s cooldown that zones you off a wave; step off the burn and everything else you beat.

edits.before: Drop Miasma to slow and poison him when he commits, denying his W move-speed escape and feeding your E
edits.after: Drop Miasma to slow and poison him when he commits — he has no dash, so the slow is what holds him

edits.before: Bait his Equalizer (R), step off the burn lines, then re-engage on its long cooldown while he has no answer
edits.after: Bait The Equalizer (R), step off the burn, then re-engage on the 130s cooldown while he has no answer

edits.before: Hit an overheat-empowered Flamespitter for the bonus damage and rely on W's shield and speed to disengage
edits.after: Hit you with a Danger Zone Flamespitter for bonus damage, then Scrap Shield's shield and speed to disengage

edits.before: You hard out-DPS an AP bruiser whose only escape is W's speed burst — your Q slow and Miasma cancel it and lock him in Twin Fang range.
edits.after: You hard out-DPS an AP bruiser whose only escape is Scrap Shield's speed burst — Miasma's slow beats it and locks him in Twin Fang range.

edits.before: This is your lane to take over. He has to step into your Q poison to land Flamespitter, and every step in is a refunded chain of Twin Fangs — your sustained DPS beats his burn duration in any extended trade. Use Miasma to slow and poison him when he over-commits or pops W to walk you down; the cloud both feeds your E and kills his speed boost. His only real bite is level 6 Equalizer: respect the two burn lines, step off them, and he has nothing for a long cooldown.
edits.after: This is your lane to take over. He has to step inside a 600-range cone to land Flamespitter, and every step in is a 0.75s Twin Fang chain — your sustained DPS beats his burn in any extended trade. He has no dash, so Miasma's grounding does nothing here; it is its slow plus your Serpentine Grace speed that keeps him out of the cone. His real punish window is Overheat: at 100% Heat he cannot cast at all for a few seconds, so bait the Heat bar full and walk in on it.

edits.before: You out-scale him hard single-target — he is an AP bruiser whose only escape is W's move-speed burst, and your Q slow plus Miasma shut that down so he can't peel off your ramping Twin Fang. Your passive move speed lets you kite the short Flamespitter cone all day while you shred him. Just track his Equalizer for objectives and fights; off cooldown he is a free target for your poison-into-Twin-Fang combo.
edits.after: You out-scale him hard single-target — he is an AP bruiser whose only escape is Scrap Shield's speed burst, and Miasma's slow beats it, so he cannot peel off your ramping Twin Fang. Serpentine Grace lets you kite the 600-range Flamespitter cone all day while you shred him. Just track The Equalizer for objectives; on its 130s cooldown he is a free target for your poison-into-Twin-Fang combo.
